67207.text: Time period of a simple pendulum is T₁ when on the earth's surface and T₂ when taken to a height '2R' above the earth's surface, where 'R' is the radius of the earth. The ratio T₁ : T₂ is
67207.sol: The time period of a simple pendulum is given by T = 2 L g . The acceleration due to gravity at a distance r from the center of the earth is g = GM r^2 . Substituting this into the time period formula gives T = 2 L r^2 GM , which implies T r . On the surface of the earth, the distance from the center is r₁ = R , so T₁ R . At a height h = 2R above the surface, the distance from the center is r₂ = R + 2R = 3R , so T₂ 3R . The ratio of the time periods is T₁ T₂ = R 3R = 1 3 . Thus, T₁ : T₂ = 1 : 3 . Answer: 1 : 3

71189.text: During pregnancy, the second trimester ranges from:
71189.sol: Human pregnancy has an average duration of about 40 weeks, which is divided into three trimesters. The first trimester ranges from the 1^ st week to the 12^ th week. 71915.subject: Chemistry
71915.text: Which of the following is a polyamide polymer?
71915.sol: Nylon-6,6 is a condensation polymer formed by the reaction of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid. During this polymerization, amide linkages ( -CO-NH- ) are formed between the monomers. Therefore, Nylon-6,6 is classified as a polyamide polymer. Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) and polythene are addition polymers. Bakelite is a phenol-formaldehyde resin, which is a cross-linked condensation polymer but does not contain amide linkages. Answer: Nylon-6,6

80699.text: The electrolytic reduction of nitrobenzene in strongly acidic medium produces:

80965.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct?

Besides it resembles angiosperms in several other aspects like presence of tetrasporic embryo sac, free nuclear divisions in the embryo sac, two cotyledonous embryo etc.

122586.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : Crocodiles are classified under Class Reptilia despite possessing a four-chambered heart. Reason (R) : They possess a creeping mode of locomotion, dry cornified skin, and epidermal scutes, which are defining features of reptiles. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate an
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
122586.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because crocodiles belong to Class Reptilia, yet they are an exception to the general reptilian feature of a three-chambered heart, as they possess a four-chambered heart. Reason (R) is also correct and provides the correct explanation for the Assertion. The classification of an organism into a particular class is based on a combination of fundamental morphological and anatomical features. Crocodiles exhibit the primary defining characteristics of reptiles, such as a creeping or crawling mo

122606.subject: Botany
122606.text: Select the option that correctly matches characteristic features with the group of three animals.
options: Skeleton of spicules - Sycon, Adamsia, Spongilla
Excretion by flame - Taenia, Fasciola, cells Ancylostoma
122606.sol: In poriferans, the body is supported by a skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibres. Sycon and Spongilla are examples of poriferans, whereas Adamsia is a coelenterate. In platyhelminths, specialised cells called flame cells help in excretion. Taenia and Fasciola are platyhelminths whereas Ancylostoma is an aschelminth. In molluscs, mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding called radula. Dentalium and Octopus are molluscs whereas Ophiura is an echinoderm. Arthropods have jointed appendages. Limulus,

122832.subject: Botany
122832.text: Select the correct set of examples for the given figure.
122832.sol: In the hypogynous flower the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior, e.g., mustard, china rose and brinjal.

122987.subject: Botany
122987.text: Which of the following plants exhibits twisted aestivation in its corolla and axile placentation in its ovary?
122987.sol: Twisted aestivation is seen in plants where one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one, and so on. Examples include China rose, lady's finger, and cotton. Axile placentation occurs when the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary. Examples include China rose, tomato, and lemon. Therefore, China rose exhibits both twisted aestivation and axile placentation. Pea has vexillary aestivation and marginal placentation. Tomato has valvate aestivation and axile placentation

123059.subject: Botany
123059.text: Which of the following represents the correct floral formula for Pisum sativum?
options: % , Bisexual, K _ (5) C _ 1+2+2 A _ (9)+1 G ₁
% , Bisexual, K _ (5) C _ 1+2+(2) A ₁₀ G ₁
123059.sol: Pisum sativum (garden pea) belongs to the family Fabaceae. The flowers of Fabaceae are zygomorphic ( % ) and bisexual. The calyx consists of 5 united sepals ( K _ (5) ). The corolla is papilionaceous, consisting of 5 petals: 1 standard, 2 wings, and 2 fused keel petals ( C _ 1+2+(2) ). The androecium consists of 10 stamens which are diadelphous ( A _ (9)+1 ). The gynoecium is monocarpellary with a superior ovary ( G ₁ ). Therefore, the correct floral formula is % , Bisexual, K _ (5) C _ 1+2+(2) A _ (9)+1 G ₁ . Answ

123219.subject: Botany
123219.text: What is the name of the innermost layer of the cortex?
123219.sol: The outermost layer is epiblema. Many of the cells of epiblema protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs. The cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells with intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of casparian strips. Next to endod

123238.subject: Botany
123238.text: What is the outermost protective layer of a leaf?
123238.sol: The vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system. The epidermis which covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of the leaf has a conspicuous cuticle . The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. The latter may even lack stomata. The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll. Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and

123412.subject: Botany
123412.text: Read the following statements regarding the anatomy of a dicotyledonous root: Statement I: The innermost layer of the cortex is the endodermis. Statement II: Root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epiblema. Statement III: Lateral roots originate exogenously from the epiblema. Statement IV: Vascular cambium in dicot roots is partly primary and partly secondary in origin. How many of the above statements are cor
123412.sol: Statement I is correct: The cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells, and its innermost layer is the endodermis. Statement II is correct: The outermost layer of the root is the epiblema. Many of its cells protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs. Statement III is incorrect: Lateral roots have an endogenous origin as they arise from the pericycle, which is located deep within the root. Statement IV is incorrect: In dicot roots, the vascular cambium is completely secondary in origin. It

123466.subject: Botany
123466.sol: Companion cells are narrow, elongated and thin walled living cells. They lie on the sides of the sieve tubes and are closely associated with them through compound plasmodesmata.

123775.subject: Botany
123775.text: The cell division of cytoplasm that occurs during the M phase of the cell cycle is called ___.
123775.sol: The cell division of cytoplasm that occurs during the M phase of the cell cycle is called Cytokinesis

123836.subject: Botany
123836.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I List-II (A) Zygotene (I) Terminalisation of chiasmata (B) Pachytene (II) Appearance of recombination nodules (C) Diplotene (III) Formation of synaptonemal complex (D) Diakinesis (IV) Appearance of X-shaped chiasmata Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123836.sol: During Prophase-I of meiosis, different substages are characterised by specific cytological events: Zygotene (A) is characterised by the pairing of homologous chromosomes (synapsis) and the formation of the synaptonemal complex (III). Pachytene (B) is marked by the appearance of recombination nodules (II), which are the sites of crossing over. Diplotene (C) begins with the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex, and the homologous chromosomes separate except at the sites of crossovers, forming X-shaped structures

124132.subject: Botany
124132.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Bacterial flagellum is composed of three parts Reason: The filament is the longest portion of flagellum
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
124132.sol: Bacterial flagellum is composed of three parts – filament, hook and basal body.

124175.subject: Botany
124175.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Prokaryotic cells lack membrane bound organelles 2. Eukaryotic cells contain membrane bound organelles 3. Mitochondria produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell. 4. Ribosomes are only found in eukaryotic cells. 5. In both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, a semi-fluid matrix called cytoplasm occupies t
124175.sol: Besides the nucleus, the eukaryotic cells have other membrane bound distinct structures called organelles like the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the golgi complex, lysosomes, mitochondria, microbodies and vacuoles. The prokaryotic cells lack such membrane bound organelles.

124316.subject: Botany
124316.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding plastids and their stored contents. List-I List-II (A) Amyloplast (I) Proteins (B) Elaioplast (II) Oils and fats (C) Aleuroplast (III) Carbohydrates (starch) (D) Chromoplast (IV) Fat-soluble carotenoids Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
124316.sol: Plastids are classified based on the type of pigments or stored nutrients they contain. Amyloplasts are leucoplasts that store carbohydrates (starch), such as in potatoes. Elaioplasts are leucoplasts that store oils and fats. Aleuroplasts are leucoplasts that store proteins. Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene and xanthophylls. Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV). Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

124411.subject: Botany
124411.text: Which one is only found in plant?
124411.sol: Out of the given options, glyoxysomes are exclusively found in plant cells only. They were discovered by Breuers (1919) in endosperm of germinating seeds. They are involved in fat metabolism through glyoxylate cycle.

124467.subject: Botany
124467.sol: Vacuoles are the storage depots of cells, surrounded by a single membrane. They contain excess water, waste products, mineral elements, cell sap and sometimes a soluble pigment anthocyanin also.

124719.subject: Botany
124719.text: In some seeds, dormancy is caused by the presence of endogenous chemical inhibitors. Which of the following chemicals can be applied to remove the effect of such inhibitory substances?
124719.sol: Seed dormancy can be caused by endogenous chemical inhibitors such as abscisic acid, phenolic acids, and para-ascorbic acid. The effect of these inhibitory substances can be removed by the application of certain chemicals like gibberellic acid and nitrates. Therefore, nitrates are used to break seed dormancy, whereas abscisic acid, para-ascorbic acid, and phenolic acids act as inhibitors that cause dormancy. Answer: Nitrates

125015.subject: Botany
125015.text: What is the net gain of ATP molecules during the aerobic respiration of one molecule of glucose?
125015.sol: But this kind of assumptions are not really valid in a living system; all pathways work simultaneously and do not take place one after another; substrates enter the pathways and are withdrawn from it as and when necessary; ATP is utilized as and when needed; enzymatic rates are controlled by multiple means. Yet, it is useful to do this exercise to appreciate the beauty and efficiency of the living system in extraction and storing energy. Hence, there can be a net gain of 38 ATP molecules during aerobic respiration

125454.subject: Botany
125454.text: What happens to C4 acids in the bundle sheath cells?
options: They are broken down to release CO2 and a 3-carbon molecule.
They are used directly in the Calvin cycle.
125454.sol: The C4 acid OAA is formed in the mesophyll cells. It then forms other 4-carbon compounds like malic acid or aspartic acid in the mesophyll cells itself, which are transported to the bundle sheath cells. In the bundle sheath cells these C4 acids are broken down to release CO2 and a 3-carbon molecule . The 3-carbon molecule is transported back to the mesophyll where it is converted to PEP again, thus, completing the cycle. It then forms other 4-carbon compounds like malic acid or aspartic acid in the mesophyll cells

126207.subject: Botany
126207.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Cultivation of apomictic hybrid seeds is highly beneficial for farmers as it eliminates the need to buy fresh seeds every year. Reason (R): Apomixis is a form of sexual reproduction that leads to the segregation of desired characters in the hybrid progeny. In the light of the above statements, choo
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
126207.sol: The Assertion is true. If hybrids are made into apomicts, there is no segregation of characters in the hybrid progeny. This allows farmers to keep using the seeds produced by the hybrids to raise new crops year after year without buying expensive fresh seeds. The Reason is false because apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction (not sexual) that mimics sexual reproduction and produces seeds without fertilization, thereby preventing (not leading to) the segregation of characters. Answer: Assertion (A) is true but R

126451.subject: Botany
126451.text: What is the R group in a fatty acid?
126451.sol: Lipids are generally water insoluble. They could be simple fatty acids. A fatty acid has a carboxyl group attached to an R group. The R group could be a methyl (–CH3), or ethyl (–C2H5) or higher number of –CH2 groups (1 carbon to 19 carbons). For example, palmitic acid has 16 carbons including carboxyl carbon. Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon.

126656.subject: Botany
126656.text: Enzyme Co-factor Associated Enzyme A. NAD+ 1. Amylase B. Mg2+ 2. Hexokinase C. Zn2+ 3. Alcohol dehydrogenase D. Coenzyme A 4. Acetyl-CoA synthetase
126656.sol: NAD+ (A) is a cofactor for Alcohol dehydrogenase (III) in redox reactions. Mg2+ (B) is required by Hexokinase (II) for catalyzing phosphorylation. Zn2+ (C) is a cofactor for enzymes like Alcohol dehydrogenase (III). Coenzyme A (D) is associated with Acetyl-CoA synthetase (IV) for the synthesis of acetyl-CoA.

126889.subject: Botany
126889.text: Match the tissues/molecules mentioned in column I with those of their degrading enzymes mentioned in column II and select the correct option from the given codes.

127006.subject: Botany
127006.text: Good ozone is found in the
127006.sol: The stratosphere is the second major layer of earth's atmosphere, just above the troposhere, and below the mesosphere. It is the layer of ozone ( O ₃ ) . The ozone absorbs high energy UV-B and UV-C energy waves and breaksdown into atomic oxygen ( O ) and diatomic oxygen ( O ₂ ) .

127210.subject: Botany
options: Exploring molecular diversity for products of economic importance
Exploring genetic diversity for products of economic importance
Exploring species:level diversity for products of economic importance
127210.sol: The narrowly utilitarian arguments for conserving biodiversity are obvious; humans derive countless direct economic benefits from naturefood (cereals, pulses, fruits), firewood, fibre, construction material, industrial products (tannins, lubricants, dyes, resins, perfumes ) and products of medicinal importance. More than 25 per cent of the drugs currently sold in the market worldwide are derived from plants and 25,000 species of plants contribute to the traditional medicines used by native peoples around the world.

127418.subject: Botany
127418.text: Which of the following is an example of an ex-situ conservation strategy?
127418.sol: In-situ conservation (on-site) involves protecting endangered species within their natural habitat. Examples include national parks, biosphere reserves, wildlife sanctuaries, and sacred groves. Ex-situ conservation (off-site) involves taking threatened animals and plants out of their natural habitat and placing them in special settings where they can be protected and given special care. Examples include zoological parks, botanical gardens, and wildlife safari parks. Therefore, a wildlife safari park is an ex-situ c

128151.subject: Zoology
128151.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the morphology of a cockroach. List-I List-II (A) Tegmina (I) Prothorax (B) Hindwings (II) Mesothorax (C) Pronotum (III) Metathorax (D) Walking legs (IV) All thoracic segments Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
128151.sol: The thorax of a cockroach consists of three segments: prothorax, mesothorax, and metathorax. (A) Tegmina (forewings) arise from the mesothorax. (B) Hindwings arise from the metathorax. (C) The pronotum is the large dorsal sclerite that covers the prothorax. (D) Each of the three thoracic segments bears one pair of walking legs, meaning they are present on all thoracic segments. Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV). Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

128341.subject: Zoology
128341.text: What is the effect of adrenaline and noradrenaline on heart beat, strength of heart contraction, and rate of respiration?
options: No effect on heart beat but increases strength of heart contraction and rate of respiration
128341.sol: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine. These are commonly called as catecholamines. Adrenaline and noradrenaline are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations and are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight. These hormones increase alertness, pupilary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs), sweating etc. Both the hormones increase the heart beat , the strength of heart contraction an

128413.subject: Zoology
128413.text: Evaluate the following statements regarding hyperthyroidism : It results from excessive production of thyroid hormones. Symptoms include weight loss and increase in metabolic rate It can cause goitre. It is commonly treated with hormone replacement therapy.
128413.sol: Due to cancer of the thyroid gland or due to development of nodules of the thyroid glands, the rate of synthesis and secretion of the thyroid hormones is increased to abnormal high levels leading to a condition called hyperthyroidism which adversely affects the body physiology. Exophthalmic goitre is a form of hyperthyroidism, characterised by enlargement of the thyroid gland, protrusion of the eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate, and weight loss, also called Graves’ disease. Thyroid hormones play an important

128416.subject: Zoology
128416.text: Where are the parathyroid glands located?
options: On the anterior surface of the thyroid gland
On the posterior surface of the thyroid gland
128416.sol: In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland, one pair each in the two lobes of the thyroid gland (Figure 22.3b). The parathyroid glands secrete a peptide hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH). The secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions. Parathyroid hormone (PTH) increases the Ca2+ levels in the blood. PTH acts on bones and stimulates the process of bone resorption (dissolution/ demineralisation).

128922.subject: Zoology
128922.text: What are the three layers that each artery and vein consists of?
options: Squamous endothelium, smooth muscle, fibrous connective tissue
Squamous endothelium, elastic fibres, collagen fibres
Tunica intima, tunica media, tunica externa
Elastic fibres, squamous endothelium, fibrous connective tissue
128922.sol: The blood flows strictly by a fixed route through Blood Vessels—the arteries and veins. Basically, each artery and vein consists of three layers: an inner lining of squamous endothelium, the tunica intima , a middle layer of smooth muscle and elastic fibres, the tunica media , and an external layer of fibrous connective tissue with collagen fibres, the tunica externa. The tunica media is comparatively thin in the veins

129308.subject: Zoology
129308.text: Order of Sequence Events A. Third 1. Release of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft B. Fourth 2. Movement of the synaptic vesicles towards the membrane where they fuse with the plasma membrane C. Second 3. Entry of ions which can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron. D. First 4. Neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors, present on the post-synaptic membrane
129308.sol: When an impulse (action potential) arrives at the axon terminal, it stimulates the movement of the synaptic vesicles towards the membrane where they fuse with the plasma membrane and release their neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft. The released neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors, present on the post-synaptic membrane. This binding opens ion channels allowing the entry of ions which can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron. The new potential developed may be either excitatory or

129447.subject: Zoology
129447.text: Organ of Corti is found in
129447.sol: Organ of Corti are found in cochlear channel (internal ear) and are responsible for hearing. Ear is concerned both with hearing and balance, semicircular canals are responsible for balance when body is in motion.

129497.subject: Zoology
129497.text: What is the final part of the renal tubule before opening into the renal pelvis?
129497.sol: The renal tubule begins with a double walled cup-like structure called Bowman’s capsule, which encloses the glomerulus. Glomerulus alongwith Bowman’s capsule, is called the malpighian body or renal corpuscle (Figure 16.4). The tubule continues further to form a highly coiled network – proximal convoluted tubule (PCT). A hairpin shaped Henle’s loop is the next part of the tubule which has a descending and an ascending limb. The ascending limb continues as another highly coiled tubular region called distal convoluted

129542.subject: Zoology
129542.text: What is the role of Henle's loop and vasa recta in the renal system?
options: To maintain a concentration gradient in the medullary interstitium
129542.sol: Mammals have the ability to produce a concentrated urine. The Henle’s loop and vasa recta play a significant role in this. The flow of filtrate in the two limbs of Henle’s loop is in opposite directions and thus forms a counter current. The flow of blood through the two limbs of vasa recta is also in a counter current pattern. The proximity between the Henle’s loop and vasa recta, as well as the counter current in them help in maintaining an increasing osmolarity towards the inner medullary interstitium , i.e., fro

129728.subject: Zoology
129728.text: Which of the following physiological conditions acts as a direct stimulus for the activation of Juxtaglomerular (JG) cells to release renin?
options: An increase in body fluid volume
A fall in glomerular filtration rate (GFR)
129728.sol: According to NCERT, a fall in glomerular blood flow, glomerular blood pressure, or glomerular filtration rate (GFR) can activate the JG cells to release renin. An increase in body fluid volume switches off the osmoreceptors and suppresses ADH release. An increase in blood pressure stimulates the release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF), which acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism by causing vasodilation. Therefore, a fall in GFR is the correct stimulus for renin release. Answer: A fall in glomerular

129914.subject: Zoology
129914.text: What can be the result of fibrosis?
129914.sol: Asthma is a difficulty in breathing causing wheezing due to inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles. Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which alveolar walls are damaged due to which respiratory surface is decreased. One of the major causes of this is cigarette smoking. Occupational Respiratory Disorders: In certain industries, especially those involving grinding or stone-breaking, so much dust is produced that the defense mechanism of the body cannot fully cope with the situation. Long exposure can give rise to inf

130026.subject: Zoology
130026.text: What will be the pO2 and pCO2 in the atmospheric air compared to those in the alveolar air?
130026.sol: the pO2 and pCO2 in the atmospheric air compared to those in the alveolar air will be pO2 higher, pCO2 lesser

130537.subject: Zoology
130537.text: Which of the following assists in the locomotion of the organism stated?
130537.sol: Hirudinaria belongs to class Hirudinea of phylum-Annelida. It has definite number of body segments (26+7=33) . It feeds on blood (sanguivorous) and has anticoagulant hirudin in its saliva. Hirudinaria have a posterior sucker for locomotion. Leech creep by looping and swim by undulations of body.

130706.subject: Zoology
130706.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Surgical methods of contraception is also called barrier 2. IUDs can be inserted without any doctor or nurse 3.Pills can be taken by males 4. Sterilisation is a terminal method to avoid pregnancies
130706.sol: Surgical methods, also called sterilisation, are generally advised for the male/female partner as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies.

130783.subject: Zoology
130783.text: Which of the following sets contains only non-hormonal contraceptive methods?
130783.sol: To identify the strictly non-hormonal methods, we must eliminate any method that relies on hormones or alters the hormonal milieu. Option 1 is incorrect because lactational amenorrhea relies on high prolactin levels to suppress gonadotropins. Option 2 is incorrect because 'Saheli' is an oral contraceptive pill that, despite being a non-steroidal preparation, modulates estrogen receptors to prevent implantation. Option 4 is incorrect because LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD. Option 3 is correct. Diaphragms are phys

131212.subject: Zoology
131212.text: A 28-year-old woman misses her menstrual period, and a subsequent urine test confirms her pregnancy by detecting the presence of a specific hormone. Identify the primary tissue source of this hormone and its immediate target structure in her ovary, respectively.
131212.sol: A positive pregnancy urine test detects the presence of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG). During pregnancy, the placenta acts as an endocrine tissue and secretes hCG. The primary function of hCG in early pregnancy is to maintain the corpus luteum in the maternal ovary. The maintained corpus luteum continues to secrete large amounts of progesterone, which is essential to sustain the endometrium and the pregnancy. Therefore, the source of the hormone is the placenta, and its immediate target in the ovary is the cor

131234.subject: Zoology
131234.text: During oogenesis, the secondary oocyte is released from the Graafian follicle during ovulation. Which of the following correctly describes the chromosomal configuration of this cell?
options: It is haploid with 23 chromosomes, each having a single chromatid.
It is haploid with 23 chromosomes, each having two sister chromatids.
It is diploid with 46 chromosomes, each having a single chromatid.
It is diploid with 46 chromosomes, each having two sister chromatids.
131234.sol: A secondary oocyte is formed after the completion of Meiosis I, which is a reductional division. Therefore, it is a haploid cell containing 23 chromosomes. At the time of ovulation, the secondary oocyte is arrested in Metaphase II of Meiosis II. Because the centromeres have not yet split (which happens during Anaphase II), each of the 23 chromosomes still consists of two sister chromatids. The separation into single chromatids only occurs after fertilization when Meiosis II is completed to form the ovum. Confusing

131507.subject: Zoology
131507.text: What is the role of the structural gene in a transcription unit?
options: To initiate the process of transcription
To define the boundaries of the region of DNA that would be transcribed
To encode the information for the synthesis of a particular protein
To prevent RNA from being translated into protein
131507.sol: The promoter and terminator flank the structural gene in a transcription unit. The promoter is said to be located towards the 5' -end (upstream) of the structural gene (the reference is made with respect to the polarity of the coding strand). It is a DNA sequence that provides binding site for RNA polymerase, and it is the presence of a promoter in a transcription unit that also defines the template and coding strands. By switching its position with terminator, the definition of coding and template strands could be

131758.subject: Zoology
131758.text: The fact that a purine base always pairs through hydrogen bonds with a pyrimidine base in the DNA double helix leads to:
131758.sol: The fact that a purine base always pairs through hydrogen bonds with a pyrimidine base in the DNA double helix leads to uniform width throughout DNA along the double helix.

131919.subject: Zoology
131919.text: In eukaryotes, identify the specific RNA polymerases responsible for the transcription of 18S rRNA, hnRNA, and 5S rRNA, respectively.
options: RNA polymerase I, RNA polymerase II, and RNA polymerase I
RNA polymerase I, RNA polymerase III, and RNA polymerase II
RNA polymerase I, RNA polymerase II, and RNA polymerase III
RNA polymerase III, RNA polymerase II, and RNA polymerase I
131919.sol: In the eukaryotic nucleus, there are three distinct RNA polymerases with specific roles: 1. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, and 5.8S). 2. RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, the heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA). 3. RNA polymerase III is responsible for the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs. Therefore, the correct sequence of enzymes for 18S rRNA, hnRNA, and 5S rRNA is RNA polymerase I, RNA polymerase II, and RNA polymerase III, respectively. A common mistake is assuming all

132152.subject: Zoology
132152.text: What phenotype is produced by bb homozygotes in pea seeds?
132152.sol: For example, starch synthesis in pea seeds is controlled by one gene. It has two alleles (B and b). Starch is synthesised effectively by BB homozygotes and therefore, large starch grains are produced. In contrast, bb homozygotes have lesser efficiency in starch synthesis and produce smaller starch grains . After maturation of the seeds, BB seeds are round and the bb seeds are wrinkled. Heterozygotes produce round seeds, and so B seems to be the dominant allele. But, the starch grains produced are of intermediate si

132430.subject: Zoology
132430.text: Given below is a list of genetic disorders : (a) Haemophilia (b) Cystic fibrosis (c) Down's syndrome (d) Colour blindness (e) Turner's syndrome (f) Klinefelter's syndrome Choose the option that correctly identifies only the chromosomal disorders :
132430.sol: Genetic disorders are broadly grouped into two categories: Mendelian disorders and Chromosomal disorders. Mendelian disorders are mainly determined by alteration or mutation in a single gene. Haemophilia, Cystic fibrosis, and Colour blindness are examples of Mendelian disorders. Chromosomal disorders are caused due to the absence or excess or abnormal arrangement of one or more chromosomes. Down's syndrome (Trisomy 21 ), Turner's syndrome ( 45 , XO ), and Klinefelter's syndrome ( 47 , XXY ) are examples of chromoso

132896.subject: Zoology
132896.text: Which of the following statements regarding human evolution is incorrect?
options: Homo habilis had a brain capacity of 650-800 cc and probably ate meat.
Australopithecines hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit.
Homo erectus lived about 1.5 million years ago and had a brain capacity of 900 cc.
Pre-historic cave art developed about 18,000 years ago.
132896.sol: According to NCERT, the first human-like hominid was Homo habilis , with a brain capacity between 650-800 cc, and they probably did not eat meat. Thus, the statement claiming they probably ate meat is incorrect. Australopithecines hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit. This statement is correct. Homo erectus appeared about 1.5 mya and had a large brain around 900 cc. This statement is correct. Pre-historic cave art developed about 18,000 years ago. This statement is also correct. Answer: Homo habilis

132905.subject: Zoology
132905.text: Which of the following examples correctly represents the phenomenon of adaptive radiation?
options: Darwin's finches in the Galapagos Islands
132905.sol: Adaptive radiation is the process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and radiating to other habitats. A classic example of this phenomenon is Darwin's finches in the Galapagos Islands. Flippers of penguins and dolphins are an example of convergent evolution (analogous structures). Industrial melanism in moths is an example of natural selection. Antibiotic-resistant bacteria represent evolution by anthropogenic action. Answer: Darwin's finches in the Galapagos Island

132917.subject: Zoology
132917.text: The placental flying squirrel and the marsupial flying phalanger have both evolved membranous extensions for gliding in their respective forest habitats. Identify the type of evolution shown by them and the nature of their gliding structures.
132917.sol: The placental flying squirrel and the marsupial flying phalanger are distantly related mammals that evolved in isolated geographical areas. They have developed similar phenotypic adaptations (membranous extensions for gliding) to survive in similar forest habitats. 95679.subject: Botany
95679.text: Organisms called methanogens are most abundant in
95679.sol: Methanogenic archaea reside primarily in the rumen and the lower segments of the intestines of ruminants, where they utilize the reducing equivalents derived from rumen fermentation to reduce carbon dioxide, formic acid or methylamines to methane (CH 4 ).

96089.subject: Botany
96089.text: Which of the following is not present in the stroma of chloroplast?
96089.sol: The stroma of chloroplast consists of double-stranded DNA, ribosomes of 70S type (smaller than cytoplasmic ribosomes which are 80S) and all enzymes for the dark reaction or Calvin cycle of photosynthesis.

96582.subject: Botany
96582.text: In which of the following ecosystem, productivity is about 55 million tonnes?
96582.sol: Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 percent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons.

96969.subject: Botany
96969.text: In which of these options, the plants are correctly matched with the modification seen in them? Phylloclade Phyllode Cladode (i) Opuntia Asparagus Acacia (ii) Casuarina Opuntia Asparagus (iii) Euphorbia Asparagus Casuarina (iv) Euphorbia Opuntia Acacia
96969.sol: Phylloclade is green photosynthetic flattened or rounded succulent stem with reduced leavesmodified into spines. Phylloclade is seen in Opuntia, Casuarina, Euphorbia, Cactus. Cladode is a also a modification of stem which usually is one or two internodes long and is succulent. Cladode is seen in Asparagus and Ruscus.Phyllode is a modification of leaf in which its petiole becomes flat and functions as normal leaf. It is seen in Australian acacia.

97180.subject: Botany
97180.text: Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during ripening of fruits, this rise in rate of respiration is called
97180.sol: Ethylene promotes senescence and abscission of plant organs especially of leaves and flowers. Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during ripening of the fruits. This rise in rate of respiration is called respiratory climactic.

97537.subject: Botany
97537.text: Which of the following character is wrong regarding brown algae?
options: They remain attached to the surface by holdfast
Presence of fucoxanthin which gives brown colour
97537.sol: Chlorophyll 'a' and 'b' are the main pigments of green algae, chlorophyll 'a', and chlorophyll 'c' is the main pigments present in brown algae. In addition, they have xanthophyll, fucoxanthin which gives them a brown color. Their body is differentiated into holdfast by which they remain attached to the surface, they have stem-like cylindrical stipe and leaf-like blade.

97693.subject: Botany
97693.text: Which of the following statement about anaerobic respiration is incorrect?
options: In animal cells, like muscles during exercise, when oxygen is inadequate for cellular respiration pyruvic acid
The net gain of ATP is 2 molecules.
In this process, less than seven percent of the energy in glucose is released.
If the concentration of alcohol is seven percent, it becomes toxic to yeast.
97693.sol: Yeasts poison themselves to death when the concentration of alcohol reaches about 13 percent.

97825.subject: Botany
97825.text: The serial arrangement of taxon/taxonomic category is known as
97825.sol: Category is rank or level in the hierarchical classification of organisms. Classification is the arrangement of organisms or groups of organisms in distinct categories in accordance with a particular and well established plan. Taxonomy is the branch of biology which deals with the collection, identification, nomenclature, description and classification of plants and animals.

98265.subject: Chemistry
98265.text: Which of the following is the simplest amino acid?
98265.sol: Glycine is considered as the simplest amino acid as it has one amino group, one carboxylic group, one hydrogen and another hydrogen in place or R-group. It has no substituent functional group. It is also not an alpha amino acid.

98278.subject: Chemistry
98278.text: Which of the following statements regarding enzyme inhibition is correct?
options: Non-competitive inhibition of an enzyme can be overcome by adding large amount of substrate
Competitive inhibition is seen when a substrate competes with an enzyme for binding to an inhibition protein
Competitive inhibition is seen when the substrate and the inhibitor compete
Non-competitive inhibitors often bind to the enzyme irreversibly
98278.sol: Competitive inhibition is seen, when the substrate and the inhibitor compete for the same active site on enzyme as their structures are similar.

98437.subject: Chemistry
98437.text: The major role of minor elements inside living organisms is to act as
options: building blocks of important amino acids
98437.sol: The micronutrients or the minor elements are the ones which are not required in large quantities. The minerals required can be either macronutrients or micronutrients. Macronutrients are the elements which are required in large amounts like carbohydrates, proteins, fats whereas micronutrients are those which mainly act as a co-factor of enzymes. Eg: Copper acts as a co-factor of the enzyme cytochrome oxidase, iron is needed by the enzyme catalase etc.
